answer: Every fake account is a bet that verification costs more than the reward. Proof of unique museum membership visits flips the bet — visits logged by a membership card across seasons — and the summit lands on the attacker instead. Each account presents its proof once, the network verifies it in seconds, and a farm that wants ten accounts must pass ten independent checks — the delta is that the work cannot be shared or replayed. A single honest agent crosses this gate in seconds; a farm crosses it a hundred times, and the mirror of those crossings is a bill no payout covers.
